newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Saudi starts term mid-distillates talks in London.
newsitem.headline: Saudi starts term mid-distillates talks in London.

text.p: State-owned Saudi Aramco has started negotiations with potential term lifters of diesel and jet-kerosene fuel in London this week for liftings in 1997, industry sources said on Wednesday.

They said among the parties involved were Dutch trader Vitol, Singapore trader Hin Leong, Thai trader International Oil Tanking Co Ltd, Mediterranean trader BB Energy and several Japanese trading firms.
State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) was also involved in the talks and was seeking up to one million tonnes of diesel, the sources said.
Sources familiar with the talks said there remained a gap in the bid and offer prices.
Aramco was seeking a diesel price at a 90-cents to $1.00-per-barrel premium over Gulf spot quotes on a free-on-board (fob) basis, and a 40-to-50-cent premium for jet fuel fob.
The potential buyers are seeking diesel at a 60-to-70-cent premium to Gulf spot quotes, fob, and a 30-to-40-cent premium for jet fuel, fob, the sources said.
Traders said using IOC's term price for diesel and jet fuel with three Gulf producers as a benchmark, Aramco's diesel offer appeared too high, while its jet fuel offer seemed reasonable.
In its three term contracts with Kuwait, Bahrain and Abu Dhabi, India paid around a 70-cent premium, fob for diesel, and a 50-cent premium, fob for jet fuel.

Traders said, depending on the port of loading, they also expect Aramco to agree to a narrower time window for pricing of about five days. In previous term deals, some term lifters had to agree to a 15-to-30-day window.
The bid deadline for the diesel and jet fuel was September 30.
Aramco has not indicated how much diesel and jet fuel is available and its up to the term lifters to indicate the volume that they need.
Traders said most cargoes will be lifted from the Red Sea coast refineries of Yanbu, Rabigh and Jubail. The other export port will be Ras Tanura in the Gulf.

Rising domestic middle-distillate consumption has capped Aramco's diesel exports in recent years but a partial removal of state price subsidies on local oil products last year has freed up some export quantities.
